Professor '''Shari L. Forbes''' (born 15 October 1977) is an Australian and Canadian forensic scientist and researcher. She is a [[thanatology]] expert on the decomposition of human bodies. She created a [[body farm]] in Australia and between 2019 and 2022 established a similar facility in Canada, connected to the Forensic Science department at Université du Québec à Trois-Rivières ([[UQTR]]).<ref name="uqtr">{{Cite web |title=La décomposition humaine se poursuit même en hiver, découvre l'UQTR |url=https://www.journaldemontreal.com/2021/05/17/la-decomposition-humaine-se-poursuit-meme-en-hiver-decouvre-luqtr-1 |access-date=2023-01-22 |website=Journal de Montreal |language=fr}}</ref> As of January 2023, she is a full professor in chemistry and biochemistry at the University of Windsor, and is hoping to start the first body farm in Ontario in the coming years.<ref name="windsor">{{Cite web |title=Windsor Gains Expertise |url=https://www.uwindsor.ca/dailynews/2022-09-16/uwindsor-gains-expertise-bats-brains-and-body-farms |access-date=2023-01-22 |website=University of Windsor |language=en}}</ref>

==Life==

Forbes was born in 1977 in [[Brewarrina]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Congress |first=The Library of |title=LC Linked Data Service: Authorities and Vocabularies (Library of Congress) |url=http://id.loc.gov/authorities/names/n2016187187.html |access-date=2020-04-19 |website=id.loc.gov}}</ref> Her family were graziers where the death of animals was routine. She completed her schooling at [[Hornsby Girls' High School]] in Sydney.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.smh.com.au/national/nsw/lunch-with-new-body-farm-queen-shari-forbes-20150401-1mcw6l.html|title=Lunch with new body farm queen, Shari Forbes|last=Power|first=Julie|date=2015-04-10|website=The Sydney Morning Herald|language=en|access-date=2020-04-19}}</ref> Her first degree was in Applied Chemistry and Forensic Science and she went on to a science based doctorate.<ref name=sydney>{{Cite web|url=https://www.uts.edu.au/staff/shari.forbes|title=Shari Forbes|website=University of Technology Sydney|language=en|access-date=2020-04-19}}</ref>

In 2005 she was involved in developing a forensic science course at the [[University of Ontario Institute of Technology]]. In 2011 she left to take up work in Australia.<ref name=canada/> She became a professor at the [[University of Sydney]].<ref name=sydney/>

Up to 2018 she was involved in creating the Australian Facility for Taphonomic Experimental Research (Australia's first [[body farm]]) where she was involved with research into decomposing bodies.<ref name="canada" /><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Verheggen |first1=François |last2=Perrault |first2=Katelynn A. |last3=Megido |first3=Rudy Caparros |last4=Dubois |first4=Lena M. |last5=Francis |first5=Frédéric |last6=Haubruge |first6=Eric |last7=Forbes |first7=Shari L. |author7-link=Shari L Forbes |last8=Focant |first8=Jean-François |last9=Stefanuto |first9=Pierre-Hugues |date=2017-07-01 |title=The Odor of Death: An Overview of Current Knowledge on Characterization and Applications |url=https://academic.oup.com/bioscience/article/67/7/600/3858865 |journal=BioScience |language=en |volume=67 |issue=7 |pages=600–613 |doi=10.1093/biosci/bix046 |issn=0006-3568 |doi-access=free}}</ref>

In 2018 she became the Canada 150 research chair in thanatology at [[Université du Québec à Trois-Rivières|UQTR]]. Her seven-year research programme was funded at $350,000 per year and the university met the cost ($350,000) of Canada's first body farm.<ref name="canada" /> The nearest similar facility was one at [[Northern Michigan University]], but Forbes was specifically targeting a forest based site.<ref name="canada">{{Cite news|url=https://www.thespec.com/news/canada/2019/11/29/she-s-in-charge-of-canada-s-first-body-farm-and-yes-she-knows-that-s-creepy.html|title=She's in charge of Canada's first 'body farm' and yes, she knows that's creepy|date=2019-11-29|work=The Hamilton Spectator|access-date=2020-04-19|language=en|issn=1189-9417}}</ref> The new body farm is at [[Bécancour Regional County Municipality|Bécancour]] and its correct name is the "Secure Site for Research in Thanatology" (or REST[ES], in French).<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=May 22, 2019 |title=Canada's 1st forensics body farm is coming this summer |url=https://www.cbc.ca/radio/asithappens/as-it-happens-tuesday-edition-1.5143405/canada-s-1st-forensics-body-farm-is-coming-this-summer-1.5143412 |archive-url= |archive-date= |access-date=19 April 2020 |website=CBC Radio}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://oraprdnt.uqtr.uquebec.ca/pls/public/gscw031?owa_no_site=816|title=Qu'est-ce que REST[ES]?|last=|first=|date=|website=Université du Québec à Trois-Rivières|access-date=23 Jan 2023}}</ref> As of 2023 she left UQTR and is now a full professor in chemistry and biochemistry at the [[University of Windsor]].

Forbes is a [[fellow of the Royal Society]] of [[New South Wales]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.royalsoc.org.au/about-us/fellows|title=Fellows - The Royal Society of NSW|website=www.royalsoc.org.au|access-date=2020-04-19}}</ref>
